title: Day-Two Concierge Ops Bulletin — VPC & On‑Prem installs (Apr 2026)
body:
Purpose: quick sync for Day‑Two concierge activities across active VPC and on‑prem installs. These are field notes / ops bullets — use this to triage owner handoffs and capture open asks.

Attendees: Aisha (ops), Diego (network), Priya (platform), Samir (sre), Elena (customer success) + oncall for customer A/B.

TL;DR: two customers with live installs: Customer A (VPC) — networking flakiness persists (MTU/distributed NAT) causing intermittent KV cache evictions and slow tail latency; Customer B (on‑prem rack) — GPU driver drift after kernel patch; model worker OOMs under burst. Both have mitigations in flight; no customer outage, but elevated P1 risk if not closed within 48–72h.

Customer A — VPC (prod, 3 zones):
- Symptom: periodic 200–800ms tail spikes for short chat sessions (seen 04/07 evening and 04/08 morning).
- Recent change: provider performed a maintenance that rehomed the NAT gateway; we saw TCP MSS path‑MTU differences.
- Debug notes: Diego ran tcpdump and saw fragmentation; path MTU currently at 1420 for one AZ. iptables on bastion is dropping small fragments in one path.
- Workarounds applied: forced MSS clamp on LB (Priya), increased gRPC keepalive for workers, enabled prefix KV cache bypass for large prompts (quick config rollback).
- Open action: Diego to confirm provider fixes MTU propagation and remove MSS clamp once stable (owner Diego, due 2026-04-11). File: JIRA-DEPLOY-9142.

Customer B — On‑prem (edge rack, air‑gapped):
- Symptom: model-worker processes crash with CUDA driver mismatch after host kernel auto‑patch. Crash trace points to libcuda.so ABI mismatch; some nodes upgraded kernel to 5.15.0-72 while drivers on GPU nodes are pinned to nvidia-driver 495.
- Temp mitigation: pinned affected nodes with nodeSelector to isolate traffic; rolled back to previous k8s node image on 2/8 nodes.
- Long term: plan to coordinate with customer's infra team to schedule driver upgrade window; build smaller non‑blocking driver shim for graceful fallback.
- Open action: Samir to prepare driver upgrade playbook and coordinate with customer (owner Samir, due 2026-04-12). PR in review: PR-412.

Common cross-cutting items:
- KMS key rotation: customer B requested out‑of‑band KMS ops. Elena to run checklist and confirm HSM availability. (owner Elena, due 2026-04-09).
- Cert expiry: small CA cert on Customer A expires 2026-04-17 — Priya to schedule rolling cert update during maintenance window (owner Priya, due 2026-04-15).
- Observability: add token‑level SLO alert for tail latency > 250ms sustained 5m; Diego/Samir to propose thresholds (due 2026-04-13).

Risks / Notes:
- If provider MTU fix is delayed >72h, KV cache bypass will increase token cost by ~8–12% for Customer A — finance/CS flagged for notification.
- On‑prem driver upgrades carry risk of extended downtime if firmware+driver combos are incompatible; prefer canary on single rack and staging network loopback tests.

Decisions made:
- Keep MSS clamp in place until provider confirms path MTU propagation (motion approved by Diego/Priya).
- For on‑prem driver issue, do not auto‑upgrade drivers — require signed schedule with customer and SRE runbook.

Action Items (compact):
- Diego: confirm provider MTU fix and remove MSS clamp (2026-04-11).
- Samir: write driver upgrade playbook and coordinate with customer B (2026-04-12).
- Priya: schedule cert rotation window for Customer A (2026-04-15).
- Elena: KMS/HSM checklist and out‑of‑band rotation confirmation (2026-04-09).
- Aisha: consolidate post‑mortem template if either issue escalates to P1 (2026-04-13).

Follow up / next sync: quick triage standup tomorrow 09:30 PT — invite list: owners above + customer success leads. If either mitigation fails, escalate to SRE pager and open incident channel (#inc-customer-ops).

Notes to self: capture packet samples and attach pcap to JIRA; preserve node images for reproducible test; ask research infra to repro large prompt burst pattern in staging.

End of bulletin.
